Latest Update: Why electrification is the climate game changer we need

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (681 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Electrification isn't just a buzzword, it's a lever that could slash energy bills while reducing the world's dependency on coal, oil and gas.
  • According to recent reports, if fuel-importing countries "speed up the electrification of their economies considerably" they could knock more than $400 billion (€357 billion) off their energy import bills by 2035 compared with 2025 levels.
  • It has been revealed that in a nutshell, electrification means replacing technologies that burn fossil fuels such as oil and gas with electric alternatives.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Electrification isn't just a buzzword, it's a lever that could slash energy bills while reducing the world's dependency on coal, oil and gas. Which also means significantly slashing the heat-trapping CO2 emissions that are linked to flooding and extreme heat around the world.

According to recent reports, if fuel-importing countries "speed up the electrification of their economies considerably" they could knock more than $400 billion (€357 billion) off their energy import bills by 2035 compared with 2025 levels. That is according to a recent analysis by the International Energy Agency, which also found that such an acceleration could mean the world needs 18 million fewer barrels of oil per day.

It has been revealed that in a nutshell, electrification means replacing technologies that burn fossil fuels such as oil and gas with electric alternatives. That means switching from diesel cars to electric vehicles (EVs), turning off gas heating and using electricity to power heat pumps.

Recent findings suggest that but the way the electricity running these things is generated is also important. In theory, an EV using power created in a coal-heavy electricity grid could be worse for the climate than a car running on gas.

Electricity derived from renewable energy sources such as solar, wind or hydropower on the other hand produces clean power.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The booming EV market is the fastest-growing electrification sector. Globally, one in four cars sold in 2025 was electric and since 2020, international sales have increased by almost 600%.

Nonetheless, electricity only covers about 20% of final energy use in the wider global economy, including that used in businesses, factories and people's homes.

It would need to supply more than half of all power by 2050 if we are to avoid runaway heating and the more intense and extreme weather events connected to a hotter climate.

In a recent development, some industries and activities are harder to electrify than others. While it's relatively easy to switch to EVs and decarbonize buildings, some industries such as petrochemicals and steel use fossil fuels as raw materials to make products like plastics, fertilizer, detergent or steel.

In addition, while heat pumps work well for low-temperature needs, they can't replace the temperatures needed in steelmaking or cement production.

The World Resources Institute, an independent research organization, recommends hydrogen, synthetic fuels or other low-carbon alternatives as more viable options than electrification in cases such as ocean shipping and aviation.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In addition to cutting down on greenhouse gas emissions resulting in cleaner air and limiting global heating, electrification is also more efficient and cheaper in the long run.

A combustion engine in a car wastes as much as 80% of its fuel energy, mostly to turn it into heat. Only about 20% is converted to actually move the car. Electric motors, on the other hand, convert about 80% of electrical energy into motion.

As the World Resources Institute points out, running all appliances on electricity will increase electricity consumption. Yet total energy costs are likely to be lower, even if electricity becomes more expensive.

In a recent development, as electricity needs grow due to the rapid expansion of AI, data centers and the overall shift to a more electrified world, outpaced grids struggle to keep up. This is increasingly holding back the energy transition, delaying the rollout of additional renewable generation, storage capacity and electrified demand.

According to the International Energy Agency, annual grid investment has to increase by about 50% by 2030 from today's $400 billion.

There's also a major mismatch between how long it takes to set up upcoming grid infrastructure (five to 15 years), compared to renewable energy projects (one to five years), and EV charging infrastructure (one to two years).

Experts say we need smarter grids that support a two-way flow of electricity while remaining secure, stable and able to keep up with higher demand as electrification intensifies.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sean Dyche enjoyed a fine playing career as a footballer, spending time with Nottingham Forest, Watford, Millwall, and Chesterfield, but he is best known for his time as a manager at the top level.

The Englishman has taken charge of 521 games during his managerial career, with spells at Watford, Burnley, Everton, and Nottingham Forest across the Championship and Premier League.

350 of those games have come in the top flight, which has seen the 55-year-old be able to manage some top players, who have represented their countries and gone on to play at the very highest level.

Playing at the top level, Dyche has coached some top stars such as Kieran Trippier, Morgan Gibbs-White, Ashley Young, Seamus Coleman, and Elliot Anderson.

But while speaking exclusively to GIVEMESPORT, via BetSelect.co.uk, the coach known for his strong defensive style of football was asked who the most underrated player of his coaching career was up to this point, and his response was surprising.

“You know what, the thing is, when I was manager at Burnley in particular, there’s so many of them," he stated.

"I mean, the first three players I signed at Burnley – I always reference them because we signed them on free transfers. We didn’t have any money, or no real money.

In a recent development, "I brought in Scott Arfield, Tom Heaton, and Dave Jones, all on free transfers. There’s three straight off the bat. But there’ve been so many who, not necessarily underrated, but like unsung heroes. So I wouldn’t say underrated. There’s not many I’ve worked with who I think were disrespected by being underrated. I think it was more, they’re a bit more under the radar: good club players, but top pros.

"So there are three that jump off the page, mainly because those three made such a difference to the side, and yet they were three free transfers, and we got promoted that season to the Premier League.

"So I look back at that and think, well, there’s certainly three players straight away – but like I say, I must reiterate it, not necessarily underrated in a disrespectful way, more that you didn’t realise how good they were until you worked with them.”.

Heaton spent six years at Burnley working under Dyche, but his career is one that would be considered to be great for any professional. He came through the academy at Manchester United and spent a number of years out on loan, before a spell with Cardiff and Bristol City prior to joining Burnley.

Industry observers note that he then went on to play for Aston Villa, and has since returned to Man Utd in the latter years of his career, working as the third-choice shot-stopper. He also earned three caps for England.

Arfield, meanwhile, spent five years at Turf Moor working with Dyche before joining Rangers, and becoming part of the squad that won the Scottish Premiership, Scottish Cup, and reached the Europa League final.

Dave Jones joined the club at 29 and was closer to the end of his career, and spent three years with the club before moving on to Sheffield Wednesday and ending his career at Wrexham.

Sources indicate that none of the three players were ever really considered to be top-level stars, and it makes sense that Dyche names them as being underrated. But they were all hugely important to his time at Burnley, in particular, and it's clear that they made a big impression on him.

  • The SFA have been forced back to the drawing board for a second time in their efforts to introduce newly introduced proposals around youth development.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 13:49 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 14:19 EST, 26 November 2026.

The SFA have been forced back to the drawing board for a second time in their efforts to introduce newly introduced proposals around youth development.

Led by chief football officer Craig Mulholland, the aims had been geared towards ensuring more Under-21 players in Scotland gain more minutes at first-team level.

The original prepares were for two Scotland-eligible Under-21 players to start in domestic cup competitions, and for players to feature for a minimum of six per cent of all available minutes across a season in league campaigns.

When it became clear that several clubs in Scotland weren’t on board, a newly introduced watered-down version was put back on the table.

But the latest proposals have also now been met with resistance — forcing the SFA to kick the can further down the road into the new year.

There will now be no vote on the back of the upcoming AGM, with further discussions required prior to something more concrete coming to fruition for the start of next season.

SFA chief football officer Craig Mulholland has been sent back to the drawing board by clubs.

A statement from the governing body remarked: ‘The Scottish FA has been encouraged by the productive dialogue with clubs regarding proposals to harness opportunities for young homegrown talent.

‘The most recent discussions have spawned a range of additional potential innovations that all parties agree will require further consultation in order to present a consolidated package of recommendations to an SPFL member vote.

‘The passion we all have for Scottish football has been demonstrated by the public debate sparked since the all-club meeting in St Andrews, when the reality of our domestic game’s standing in respect of playing time for under-21 players compared to the rest of Europe was made clear.

‘We will continue to engage in dialogue with the aim of delivering a proposal that will achieve the stated objective of improving opportunities for young homegrown players to fulfil their potential at the top end of the Scottish professional game.

‘It is an objective everyone benefits from: players, clubs, supporters and Scotland national teams.

‘We have therefore agreed that the consultation process will continue into the Upcoming Year with the intention of a comprehensive proposal going to SPFL members within the first quarter of 2027, in time for the start of William Hill SPFL season 2027-28.

‘The Scottish FA General Meeting to vote on the complementary Scottish Gas Men’s Scottish Cup proposals will now follow a similar timetable.

‘Given the implications for our game, and our young talent, it is imperative that we take the necessary time to get those proposals right.’.

Andoni Iraola looked up to the ceiling of Fenerbahce’s media auditorium as he tried to find the words to describe the madness he had just witnessed.

Liverpool have made the long trip to Turkey to take on Fenerbahce on matchday four of the Champions League.

Liverpool enter this fixture having won all three Champions League matches thus far, beating Atletico Madrid, LASK and Villarreal to make it nine points from nine for Andoni Iraola’s side. Liverpool’s five-game unbeaten streak was ended by Arsenal in the league on Sunday. They return to the city where the club enjoyed one of their most memorable nights, beating AC Milan in the Champions League final 21 years ago.

“Istanbul is always going to be very special for Liverpool,” Iraola mentioned. “It is difficult to find a more important night. Tomorrow [tonight] it won’t be easy, you talk about statistics, especially English teams playing here. They have very good players and a very good squad, they know how to play in this competition. We have to start strong in the game. It is very early in the season to establish comparisons. We want to continue how we have done in the Champions League, three games and nine points, it is a good chance to get to 12 points and then finish in the top eight. Champions League away is very difficult.”.

In addition to the long-term absentees Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Giovanni, both Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong have missed the trip to Turkey.

Industry observers note that fenerbahce have made a slow start to their Champions League campaign, taking just two points from their opening three fixtures. They have drawn twice against Roma and Slavia Prague at home whilst they suffered a heavy 6-0 loss at Aston Villa. Former Liverpool forward Dirk Kuyt has been appointed their interim coach following the resignation of Ismail Kartal following their recent defeat to arch rivals Galatasaray just over a week ago.

In a recent development, “It is a great opportunity for us to show what we can do,” Kuyt said. “It is also a great opportunity for me, a game between two teams that are very important to me. We have a very good plan, and we have to believe in this plan. No-one who loves Fenerbahce is happy with the current situation, but this is a huge opportunity. We have players who have won the Champions League and the World Cup.”.

It has been revealed that they come into tonight’s match having lost back-to-back league games since drawing against Slavia Prague on matchday three of the Champions League. They have plenty of former Premier League players in their ranks, including Ederson, N’Golo Kante and Romelu Lukaku.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Felix Nmecha's renewed use of the "Crowns down celebration" — where a crown is pretended to be removed from someone's head and placed at Jesus' feet — has sparked a reaction from Borussia Dortmund's official supporters' group.

  • According to recent reports, "In the past, the the Borussia Dortmund supporters club has deliberately refrained from commenting on sports-related problems and the athletic performance of individual players.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Felix Nmecha's renewed use of the "Crowns down celebration" — where a crown is pretended to be removed from someone's head and placed at Jesus' feet — has sparked a reaction from Borussia Dortmund's official supporters' group.

In a recent development, "Faith does not justify exclusion. Faith does not justify division. Borussia Dortmund is a club for everyone," read a statement after the Bundesliga club beat Elversberg, a game in which Nmecha scored twice. Nmecha's first documented "Crowns down celebration" was at the 2026 World Cup, for which "The King's Return" campaign was debuted.

According to recent reports, "In the past, the the Borussia Dortmund supporters club has deliberately refrained from commenting on sports-related problems and the athletic performance of individual players. We remain committed to this approach," the statement continued.

"However, when it comes to our club's values, discrimination, and the question of what view of humanity is fostered within and around Borussia Dortmund, we cannot and will not remain silent.".

The fan club states their issue is not with Nmecha being a devout Christian, but rather his public support for "The King's Return" campaign, which the supporters club stated "gives us cause to reassess the situation.".

According to recent reports, this campaign, according to research by German public broadcaster ARD in the summer of 2026, was designed by the "Ballers in God" (MASSIVE) network. BIG was founded in 2015 by footballer John Bostock, a devout Christian who wanted to create a community where professional footballers could strengthen each other in their faith, pray together, and read the Bible. In over a decade since, the BIG community has grown to nearly 800,000 followers on Instagram.

Nmecha issued a response on social media not long afterwards, writing:.

"I've been told that my most recent goal celebration has led to some misunderstandings," Nmecha wrote.

"My message was never intended to spread intolerance, discrimination, or hatred in any form. As Christians, our message is one of love and respect for every person—regardless of where someone comes from, what they believe in, or what worldview they hold.".

Reports suggest that both the board at Dortmund and Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp will speak to Nmecha on the matter in the coming days.

The fan club say their criticism is "directed at religious networks that, under the guise of faith, promote a worldview in which people are devalued or marginalized because of their sexual orientation, gender identity, lifestyle, or personal choices... When religious beliefs are used to deny people their dignity or equality, that is where our tolerance for intolerance ends.".

Here, they are referring to the recent ARD investigation. That work revealed the homepage for "The King's Return" campaign featured a link to a live counseling chat run by US-based evangelical nonprofit Groundwire. During the investigations, counselors told reporters that abortion is "Satan's blueprint" and that homosexuality is a sin.

Borussia Dortmund's statement of core values commits the club to diversity, human rights, and inclusion regardless of gender, sexual orientation, faith, or background. The club's largest and most influential fan group also promotes progressive, anti-fascist, and inclusive values. It is also part of a wider fan landscape in Germany where club members are more involved in club decisions than in many other countries. This was evidenced when the club signed a deal with arms manufacturer Rheinmetall two years ago and in the case of Nmecha as well. When the midfielder signed for Dortmund in 2023, many of the club's fans protested because the player had previously shared or liked several transphobic and homophobic posts on his Instagram account. In response, Nmecha deleted some posts and instead issued a statement emphasizing "I do not discriminate against anyone.".

Article 4 of German Basic Law guarantees that each individual is allowed to decide how strongly, why and which god to believe in. In football, players cannot display political, religious, or personal slogans, statements, or images on their jerseys, undershirts, or gear. However, physical gestures are allowed so long as they don't delay the game or antagonize the crowd.

The use of physical religious gestures has history in sports, as professor Paul Putz described in his book "The Spirit of the Game: American Christianity and Massive-Time Sports". Putz describes how the the pioneers of the Christian athlete movement realized they: "could influence others to Christian ideals more effectively on the field than in the pulpit.".

Sources indicate that and yet, such gestures can also be at odds with the atmosphere of modern sports arenas, particularly football. In their book "Sports and Christianity: Historical and Contemporary Perspectives", Nick J. Watson and Andrew Parker explain how modern sport has become a substitute for traditional faith.

"Sport seduces the teeming 'global village'; it is the latest opiate of the masses; it is one of the great modern experiences … Sport, for many, has replaced religion as a source of emotional catharsis and spiritual passion," they wrote.

With the 26-year-old Nmecha a key player for both club and country, the conversation around faith and football looks set to continue for some time yet.

UEL | Olympiacos 2-4 Milan: Hutchinson inspiration for epic comeback

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (707 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Football-italia

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Omari Hutchinson kept Milan’s Europa League hopes alive by inspiring the 4-2 comeback win away to Olympiacos with a goal and two assists for Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic, then Diego Moreira late on.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Omari Hutchinson kept Milan’s Europa League hopes alive by inspiring the 4-2 comeback win away to Olympiacos with a goal and two assists for Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic, then Diego Moreira late on.

The Rossoneri had a terrible record in the Europa League, losing three of their four matches without finding the net, with a 4-0 victory away to RB Salzburg the outlier. They made the trip to Greece without Luka Modric, Francesco Camarda, Davide Bartesaghi, Strahinja Pavlovic, Samuel Chukwueze, Matteo Gabbia, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Alexis Saelemaekers and Pietro Terracciano, so squad rotation was kept to a minimum.

Olympiacos were still unbeaten with three wins and a draw, but missed Leon Bailey, Chiquinho, Gustavo Puerta and Santiago Hezze are out, plus long-term absentees and cup-tied Yusuf Yazici, Balsa Popovic, Ayoub El Kaabi, Marius Mouandilmadji, Clayton, Joel Roca and Lorenzo Scipioni.

See how it all unfolded on the Liveblog.

Diego Moreira was valuable in defence during the opening minutes when charging down the Martins effort after a Panagiotis Retsos cross from the right.

Gelson Martins had a couple of pops from distance, but the first real chance was on 22 minutes with a curler that Maignan flew to palm around the upright.

Recent findings suggest that olympiacos were increasing the pressure and broke the deadlock with former Inter defender and Italy Under-21 international Pirola’s header, in off the underside of the crossbar from a Gustavo Sa corner. UEFA credited it as a Maignan own goal because the ball hadn’t completely crossed the line until it hit the goalkeeper on the way off the bar.

Pirola was every bit as decisive four minutes later, because Alphadjo Cisse had sprinted away on the counter, was tackled by the on-rushing goalkeeper, but still managed to prod it towards the empty net, only for the Italian defender to rush back for a desperate goal-line clearance.

It should’ve been 2-0 in added time, as Bruno Onyemaechi pulled back from the left for Pirola to fire over undisturbed from 10 yards.

According to recent reports, milan introduced Christian Pulisic and Yunus Musah for the restart, but instead went 2-0 down. Maignan made the save on the Joao Silva angled drive, but as the move continued, the same player ran onto the Freuler through ball to blast into the roof of the net from just inside the area.

Just as Olympiacos were pouring forward for a third, they were caught by a rapid counter-attack. Hutchinson started the move from inside his own half, rode two tackles and cut inside to drill low into the far bottom corner to give Milan some hope.

Hutchinson contributed to the equaliser too as the comeback was completed, his cross from the right finding Cisse to squirm away from his marker to nod in at the back post.

Industry observers note that hutchinson was simply unstoppable in the second half when used out wide on the right, and he provided his second assist to turn the game around, met by the fantastic Pulisic volley from 12 yards with the right boot. It was the American’s fifth goal in his last six appearances.

Incredible work from Omari Hutchinson, who sets up Christian Pulisic for a fine volley 👌.

— Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) November 26, 2026.

Cisse’s acrobatic bicycle kick didn’t quite come off from yet another Hutchinson cross, while Pirola’s risky interception prevented Adrien Rabiot meeting the Moreira assist.

In the final minute, penalty appeals were rejected because a header was charged down by Fikayo Tomori’s shoulder, but then Milan wasted the chance to add a fourth on the counter with Pulisic ballooning over.

With the last kick of the game, Hutchinson broke away on the counter from an Olympiacos corner, sent Pulisic down the left, he rolled across for Moreira to take a touch, then sweep in from 12 yards for 4-2.

The Rossoneri had never been able to beat a Greek team away from home before, managing only four draws and two defeats, including a 3-1 loss to Olympiacos in December 2018.
